title: What Can Analogy Tell Us About Artificial Consciousness?
abstract: arXiv:2610.01002v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Who or what is conscious? Because subjective experience is directly accessible only in the first person, judgments about consciousness in other entities depend partly on analogy. Historically, such inferences have focused on nonhuman animals, but advances in artificial intelligence have raised the possibility of conscious AI. Here we develop a causal framework for evaluating such evidential analogies. The key distinction is between similarities in factors plausibly involved in generating consciousness and similarities in downstream behavioural or cognitive effects. Our framework weights source-target similarity by causal relevance while allowing for unknown causes, disabling differences and alternative routes to consciousness. Applied to biological systems, it explains why analogical support generally weakens with increasing causal distance from humans. translated_title: 类比能告诉我们关于人工智能意识的什么？
translated_abstract: 谁或什么是具有意识的？由于主观体验只有第一人称才能直接获取，对其他实体是否具有意识的判断部分依赖于类比推理。历史上，这类推理主要集中在非人类动物身上，但人工智能的进步使有意识的人工智能成为可能。在此，我们开发了一个因果框架来评估这类证据性类比。其中的关键区分在于：参与生成意识的合理因素之间的相似性，与下游行为或认知效应的相似性。我们的框架根据因果相关性对源域与目标域的相似性进行加权，同时考虑未知原因、失效差异以及通往意识的其他可能途径。将该框架应用于生物系统时，它解释了为什么类比支持通常随着与人类因果距离的增加而减弱。将该框架应用于当代人工智能时，它表明行为相似性只能提供有限的（意识证据）……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个评估意识类比推理的因果框架，通过区分生成意识的因果因素相似性与下游行为效应相似性，解释了为何生物类比随因果距离增大而减弱，并表明当代人工智能的行为相似性只能提供有限的意识证据。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a causal framework for evaluating evidential analogies about consciousness, distinguishing similarities in causally relevant factors from downstream behavioral similarities, explaining why analogical support weakens with causal distance from humans, and suggesting that behavioral similarity in contemporary AI provides only limited evidence of consciousness.
